subject: Capacity assurance: token-rate guarantees, latency targets, and measurement playbook
messages:
From: Sara Dolan <sara.dolan@axionhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps <eng-ops@axionhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@axionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity assurance: token-rate guarantees, latency targets, and measurement playbook

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we move to an internal procurement review I'd like to lock down two things for our commercial team:

1) What does Redwood guarantee in terms of sustained token-rate (tokens/sec) vs requests/sec for a Dedicated GPU pool? We have interactive endpoints with sequence lengths averaging 120 tokens and peaks during business hours.

2) How will you measure compliance to that guarantee? Specifically: measurement window, steady-state vs ramp, sample size, and how missed SLOs convert to credits. We need something we can attach to an SOW.

If you can send a short measurement playbook and a commercial band (commit size -> discount -> credit formula) that would be great. I've attached our sample load profile (axion-profile-120seq.json) — please confirm whether you need different artifacts.

Regards,
Sara
Sara Dolan
Head of Ops, Axion Health
[sent from mobile]
[attachment: axion-profile-120seq.json]
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Dolan <sara.dolan@axionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity assurance: token-rate guarantees, latency targets, and measurement playbook

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the profile. Quick response below and I attached a concise playbook and a sample benchmark CSV.

Summary (short):
- Commitment guarantees are expressed as a sustained token-rate (tokens/sec) per committed GPU-pool band, with a secondary requests/sec cap defined for short RPC-heavy bursts.
- Measurement: steady-state sampling (60s contiguous windows) collected across a 4-hour acceptance run during your peak period; SLO evaluated on p95 latency for a representative sequence length cohort (50/120/256 tokens).
- Missed SLOs convert to service credits computed as a percentage of monthly committed spend; formula included in attached PDF.

Practical sizing notes:
- For the 120-token average you supplied, our baseline mapping is: 1x A100-equivalent GPU in a Dedicated pool typically sustains ~1.2M tokens/minute (approx 20k tokens/sec) for gpt-like 7B models in FP16. Heavier models or larger context increase needs linearly.
- We size pools by conservative 95th-percentile concurrency and allow for a 30% burst headroom for <30s spikes, beyond which requests are queued or routed to fallback lower-cost variants.

Measurement playbook (high level):
1) Preparation: Redwood and Axion agree on test model version, quantization profile, and request traces (you provided).
2) Warm-up: KV cache and model hot paths warmed for 10 minutes to reach steady-state.
3) Acceptance run: 4-hour window during your identified peak; sample into contiguous 60s windows and compute tokens/sec, requests/sec, and p50/p95/p99 latencies per sequence-length cohort.
4) Stability checks: reject runs with >5% variance in tokens/sec across sampling windows (we re-run up to 2x).
5) Outcome: pass if p95 latency <= target in the SOW across the 4-hour run and tokens/sec sustained >= committed rate in >=95% of sampled 60s windows.

I've attached: axh_sample_benchmark_results.csv (sample output), measurement-script.sh (what our ops will run), and redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf (commercial language + credit calc).

Next steps: Ben will follow up on discount bands and contract language. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the measurement harness.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity assurance: token-rate guarantees, latency targets, and measurement playbook

Sara — thanks for raising this. High-level commercial proposal to pair with the technical playbook Irene sent:

Commit bands (example):
- Band A: 12-month commit, 100M tokens/month -> 18% volume discount; 3% monthly credit per missed SLO event (cap 50% of monthly spend).
- Band B: 12-month commit, 300M tokens/month -> 25% volume discount; 5% monthly credit per missed SLO event (cap 60%).
- Band C: 24-month commit, 500M tokens/month -> 32% volume discount; 7% monthly credit per missed SLO event (cap 75%).

Notes:
- Credits are tiered by severity: partial degradation (tokens/sec drop between 80-95% of committed) vs full degradation (<80%). Exact thresholds and credit math are in the attached PDF.
- We can include a one-time acceptance test (the 4-hour run) as a condition precedent to starting the committed billing period. If acceptance fails twice, you may exit without penalty.

Open items for procurement: final commit band, desired credit cap, and whether Axion requires additional credits for data residency or private deployment (those change pricing).

I can prepare a draft SOW and redlineable DocuSign if you want to move forward; hitting procurement goals this quarter would make our legal timelines friendly.

Best,
Ben
Director, Commercials, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sara Dolan <sara.dolan@axionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity assurance: token-rate guarantees, latency targets, and measurement playbook

Quick technical clarifications to avoid ambiguity in the SOW:

- Token-rate vs requests/sec: Our platform reports both. For regulation of the Commitment we prefer tokens/sec because it normalizes across generation length, but we'll include a concurrent requests/sec cap for short-burst scenarios. The acceptance test will report both metrics.

- Sequence-length cohorts: please confirm we should use 50/120/256 as sample cohorts. Each cohort will be run weighted according to your traffic profile (you provided weights in the profile file).

- Warm-cache behavior: the 10-minute warm-up includes a KV-cache population step that approximates your production cache hit-rate; cold-starts are not part of acceptance, but we can run separate cold-start tests and agree to fallback policies.

- Measurement windows & statistics: our ops will compute tokens/sec per contiguous 60s window, then take the 5th percentile of those window values across the 4-hour run as the conservative sustained-rate metric. SLO pass requires that this 5th-percentile >= committed token-rate.

- Latency targets: SOW should specify p50/p95 targets for each cohort. We suggest p95 <= 350ms for 50-token cohort, p95 <= 700ms for 120-token cohort, and p95 <= 1.2s for 256-token cohort (model dependent). If you'd like tighter targets we can re-run sizing with alternative model/quant settings.

I'll include an ops checklist with exact script commands and a sample CSV column layout used for acceptance. Happy to review the draft SOW.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Infra & Serving, Redwood Inference

Ben / Irene — procurement here. We reviewed the playbook and commercial bands and are broadly aligned. A couple of asks before we proceed to DocuSign:

1) Can you shorten the acceptance run to a 2-hour steady-state sampling window but increase sampling density (30s windows) so our engineering team can run acceptance during a constrained maintenance window?
2) Provide a worked example showing credit calculation for a Band B miss (we want to validate math against our finance model).
3) Add a clause that acceptance failures allow one remediation run (ops fixes) plus one re-run; if re-run fails, we will negotiate pro-rata credits or exit.

If you can provide a redlined SOW with those items and a link to DocuSign we can move fast.

Thanks,
Tom Weaver
